text:
rachel_sales: Quick presales blocker 1: prospect insists ALL inference traffic, KMS calls, and control-plane auth must stay inside an AWS Wavelength zone (us-east-1-wl9). They want: 1) BYO-KMS via a VPC endpoint, 2) a short subprocessor manifest limited to Redwood services (no third-party processing beyond the carrier), and 3) a one-off POC price for isolated tenancy. Can we support a timeboxed POC?

infra_sam: Short: compute in wl9 is viable for Dedicated/Private. However, two big constraints: (A) we don't ship a hosted control plane inside Wavelength zones today, (B) some of our agent-side telemetry defaults to sending health metrics to our control plane region. For a POC we can work around both by deploying a tiny control-plane proxy in the customer's wl9 VPC and disabling telemetry egress. That requires infra validation + a short config window.

sre_noah: Ops checklist to share with customer: - Confirm carrier/legal entity name and peering contact - Provide the BYO-KMS ARN and the VPC endpoint DNS (we need cross-account policy to allow our runtime principal) - Provide ENI / peering docs and a network diagram showing route tables and MTU - Expected QPS and max prompt length (for sizing the wl9 pool) - Decide whether they accept request rejection if wl9 capacity is exhausted (no-fallback mode)

legal_maya: We can output a Redwood-only subprocessor manifest (auth, runtime, monitoring agent, storage). Carrier/ISP subprocessors are out-of-band; we can draft a template attestation request the customer can send to the telco, but we cannot guarantee their signature. If they require contractual "carrier-only" guarantee on network path, that is a legal exception and needs a scoped DPA appendix.

ops_zoe: Sample policies we can share. Two modes: STRICT (zone-only, reject on no capacity) and PREFERRED (prefer wl9, fallback to us-east-1 with canary). Note: for STRICT we will default to disabling prefix/KV caching and token-level logs to avoid accidental egress. If the customer provides a shared disk inside wl9 we can enable caching but that must be approved.

STRICT example (yaml):
```yaml
routing_policy:
  mode: "zone-only"
  preferred_zone: "us-east-1-wl9"
  fallback: []
  byo_kms: true
  kms_vpc_endpoint: "vpce-0123456789abcdef0"
  telemetry: "off"
  kv_cache: "disabled"
  enforcement: "reject-on-no-capacity"
```

PREFERRED example (json):
```json
{
  "routing_policy": {
    "preferred_zone": "us-east-1-wl9",
    "fallback_sequence": ["us-east-1"],
    "require_byo_kms": true,
    "kms_vpc_endpoint": "vpce-0123456789abcdef0",
    "canary": true,
    "kv_caching": "disabled",
    "telemetry_mode": "minimal"
  }
}
```

ops_zoe: Operational caveats to call out in the email to the customer: 
- control-plane proxy: lightweight but required if they disallow control-plane egress (adds ~3 business days)
- BYO-KMS: provide exact ARN + VPC endpoint + cross-account policy allowing principal arn:aws:iam::REDACTED:role/redwood-runtime to decrypt
- observability: we will route metrics/logs to customer-managed sinks in wl9 when possible, otherwise telemetry will be disabled
- prefix/KV cache: disabled by default in strict mode unless a customer-managed shared disk is mounted inside wl9

rachel_sales: They gave carrier as "CloudWave Mobile LLC" on the RFQ and asked for a POC uplift quote for a 2-week isolated tenancy. Can ops give a ballpark?

infra_sam: Ballpark POC uplift = base dedicated rate + 30% for isolation + a flat validation fee (one-time) to cover proxy deployment and infra tests. Final depends on SKU and expected QPS; ask the customer for QPS and concurrency.

legal_maya: I'll draft a short DPA appendix for POC-only network-path language and an attestation request template for CloudWave. Send me the exact legal entity name + jurisdiction.

bot-deploy: PR-10123 created: wl9-proxy-validation (ETA 72h)

rachel_sales: Thanks. I'll collect the CloudWave PoA, the BYO-KMS vpce info, and the perf numbers (they said QPS ~10 for the POC). Will follow up with the DPA request and the STRICT policy if they insist.

(End thread)
